paragraphs.sourceText: In this section you will hear a mini-lecture. You will hear the mini-lecture ONCE ONLY. While listening to the mini-lecture, complete the gap-filling task on ANSWER SHEET ONE and write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each gap. Make sure what you fill in is both grammatically and semantically acceptable. You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在本节中，您将听到一个小型讲座。您只会听到一次迷你讲座。听迷你讲座时，完成第一张答题卡上的填空任务，并为每个空白写不超过三个单词。确保您填写的内容在语法和语义上都是可接受的。您可以使用空白纸做笔记。

paragraphs.sourceText: You have THIRTY seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您有三十秒的时间来预览填补空白的任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, listen to the mini-lecture. When it is over, you will be given THREE minutes to check your work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，请听小讲座。结束后，您将有三分钟时间检查您的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section you will hear TWO interviews. At the end of each interview, five questions will be asked about what was said. Both the interviews and the questions will be read ONCE ONLY. After each question there will be a ten-second pause. During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C and D, and mark the best answer to each question on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在本节中，您将听到两次采访。每次访谈结束时，都会针对访谈内容提出五个问题。采访和问题都只会阅读一次。每个问题后都会有十秒钟的停顿。暂停期间，您应该阅读 A、B、C、D 四个选项，并在第二张答题卡上标记每个问题的最佳答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: You have THIRTY seconds to preview the choices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您有三十秒的时间来预览选项。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, listen to the first interview. Questions 1 to 5 are based on the first interview
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，请听第一个采访。问题 1 至 5 基于第一次面试

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section there are three passages followed by fourteen multiple choice questions. For each multiple choice question, there are four suggested answers marked A, B, C and D. Choose the one that you think is the best answer and mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节由三篇文章组成，后面是十四道多项选择题。对于每个多项选择题，有四个建议答案，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。选择您认为最佳答案的一个，并将您的答案标记在答题表二上。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) If the properties of human language make it such a unique communication system, quite different from the communication systems of other creatures, then it would seem extremely unlikely that other creatures would be able to understand it. Some humans, however, do not behave as if this is the case. There is, after all, a lot of spoken language directed by humans to animals, apparently under the impression that the animal follows what is being said. Riders can say Whoa to horses and they stop. Should we treat these examples as evidence that non-humans can understand human language? Probably not. The standard explanation is that the animal produces a particular behavior in response to a particular sound-stimulus or noise, but does not actually “understand” what the words in the noise mean.
paragraphs.translationZh: （1）如果人类语言的特性使其成为一种独特的交流系统，与其他生物的交流系统截然不同，那么其他生物似乎极不可能理解它。然而，有些人的行为却并非如此。毕竟，人类有很多口语是针对动物的，显然是在动物会听从所说内容的印象下。骑手可以对马说一声“哇”，马就会停下来。我们是否应该将这些例子视为非人类可以理解人类语言的证据？可能不会。标准的解释是，动物对特定的声音刺激或噪音产生特定的行为，但实际上并不“理解”噪音中的单词的含义。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) In an early attempt to teach a chimpanzee to use human language, in the 1930s, two scientists (Luella and Winthrop Kellogg) raised an infant chimpanzee together with their baby son. The chimpanzee, called Gua, was reported to be able to understand about a hundred words, but did not “say” any of them. In the 1940s, a chimpanzee named Viki was reared by another scientist couple (Catherine and Keith Hayes) in their own home, exactly as if she were a human child. These foster parents spent five years attempting to get Viki to “say” English words by trying to shape her mouth as she produced sounds. Viki eventually managed to produce some words, rather poorly articulated versions of “mama”, “papa” and “cup”. In retrospect, this was a remarkable achievement since it has become clear that non-human primates do not actually have a physically structured vocal tract which is suitable for articulating the sounds used in speech.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 在 20 世纪 30 年代，两位科学家（卢埃拉和温思罗普·凯洛格）早期尝试教黑猩猩使用人类语言，他们将一只小黑猩猩和他们的小儿子一起抚养长大。据报道，这只名叫 Gua 的黑猩猩能够理解大约一百个单词，但不会“说出”其中任何一个。 20 世纪 40 年代，一只名叫 Viki 的黑猩猩由另一对科学家夫妇（Catherine 和 Keith Hayes）在自己家里抚养，就像她是一个人类孩子一样。这些养父母花了五年的时间试图通过在发声时塑造她的嘴型来让 Viki“说”英语单词。 Viki 最终成功地说出了一些单词，但发音相当糟糕的“妈妈”、“爸爸”和“杯子”。回想起来，这是一项了不起的成就，因为很明显，非人类灵长类动物实际上并不具有适合发出语音的物理结构声道。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) Recognizing that a chimpanzee was a poor candidate for spoken language learning, another scientist couple (Beatrix and Allen Gardner) set out to teach a female chimpanzee called Washoe to use a version of American Sign Language. This sign language has all the essential properties of human language and is learned by many congenitally deaf children as their natural first language. From the beginning, the Gardner’s and their research assistants raised Washoe like a human child in a comfortable domestic environment. Sign language was always used when Washoe was around and she was encouraged to use signs. In a period of three and a half years, Washoe came to use signs for more than a hundred words. Even more impressive was Washoe’s ability to take these forms and combine them to produce “sentences” of the type “gimme tickle”, “more fruit” and “open food drink”. Some of the forms appear to have been inventions by Washoe, as in her novel sign for “bib” and in the combination “water bird” (referring to a swan), which would seem to indicate that her communication system had the potential for productivity.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 认识到黑猩猩不适合口语学习，另一对科学家夫妇（贝娅特丽克丝和艾伦·加德纳）开始教一只名叫瓦肖的雌性黑猩猩使用一种美国手语。这种手语具有人类语言的所有基本属性，许多先天性聋哑儿童将其作为他们的自然第一语言来学习。从一开始，加德纳夫妇和他们的研究助理就在舒适的家庭环境中像人类孩子一样抚养瓦肖。当瓦肖在场时，人们总是使用手语，并且鼓励她使用手语。在三年半的时间里，瓦肖开始使用符号来表达一百多个单词。更令人印象深刻的是瓦肖能够采用这些形式并将它们组合起来产生“给我痒痒”、“更多水果”和“打开食物饮料”等类型的“句子”。其中一些形式似乎是瓦肖的发明，例如她新颖的“围脖”标志和“水鸟”（指天鹅）的组合，这似乎表明她的通信系统具有生产力的潜力。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) At the same time as Washoe was learning sign language, another chimpanzee named Sarah was being taught (by Ann and David Premack) to use a set of plastic shapes for the purpose of communicating with humans. These plastic shapes represented “words” that could be arranged in sequence to build “sentences”. The basic approach was quite different from that of the Gardner’s. Sarah was systematically trained to associate these shapes with objects or actions. She remained an animal in a cage, being trained with food rewards to manipulate a set of symbols. Once she had learned to use a large number of these plastic shapes, Sarah was capable of getting an apple by selecting the correct plastic shape (a blue triangle) from a large array. Sarah was also capable of producing “sentences” such as “Mary give chocolate Sarah” and had the impressive capacity to understand complex structures such as “If Sarah put red on green, Mary give Sarah chocolate”.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 在瓦肖学习手语的同时，另一只名叫莎拉的黑猩猩（由安和大卫·普雷马克）正在学习使用一组塑料形状来与人类交流。这些塑料形状代表“单词”，可以按顺序排列以构建“句子”。基本方法与加德纳的方法截然不同。莎拉接受过系统的训练，能够将这些形状与物体或动作联系起来。她仍然是一只关在笼子里的动物，接受食物奖励的训练来操纵一组符号。一旦莎拉学会了使用大量的塑料形状，她就能够通过从一大堆塑料形状（蓝色三角形）中选择正确的塑料形状来获得一个苹果。莎拉还能够说出“句子”，例如“玛丽给莎拉巧克力”，并且具有理解复杂结构的能力，例如“如果莎拉把红色放在绿色上，玛丽就给莎拉巧克力”。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) A psychologist Herbert Terrace argued that chimpanzees simply produce signs in response to the demands of people and tend to repeat signs those people use, yet they are treated as if they are taking part in a “conversation”. As in many critical studies of animal learning, the chimpanzees’ behavior is viewed as a type of conditioned response to cues provided by human trainers.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 心理学家赫伯特·特雷斯认为，黑猩猩只是根据人们的要求发出手势，并倾向于重复人们使用的手势，但他们却被视为正在参与“对话”。正如许多动物学习的批判性研究一样，黑猩猩的行为被视为对人类训练者提供的线索的一种条件反应。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) Important lessons have been learned from attempts to teach chimpanzees how to use forms of language. We have answered some questions. Were Washoe and Sarah capable of taking part in interaction with humans by using a symbol system chosen by humans and not chimpanzees? The answer is clearly “Yes.” Could Washoe and Sarah go on to perform linguistically on a level comparable to a two-year-old child? The answer is just as clearly “No.” In arriving at these answers, we have also had to face the fact that, even with our list of key properties, we still don’t seem to have a non-controversial definition of what counts as “using language”. It has to be fair to say that, in both cases, we observe the participants “using language”. However, there is a difference. Underlying the two-year-old’s communicative activity is the capacity to develop a highly complex system of sounds and structures, plus a set of computational procedures, which will allow the child to produce extended discourse containing a potentially infinite number of novel utterances. No other creature has been observed “using language” in this sense. It is in this more fundamental or abstract sense that we say that language is uniquely human.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 从教黑猩猩如何使用语言形式的尝试中吸取了重要的教训。我们已经回答了一些问题。瓦肖和莎拉是否能够使用人类而不是黑猩猩选择的符号系统来与人类互动？答案显然是“是”。瓦肖和莎拉能否继续达到与两岁孩子相当的语言水平？答案显然是“不”。在得出这些答案时，我们还必须面对这样一个事实：即使我们列出了关键属性，我们似乎仍然没有对什么是“使用语言”有一个没有争议的定义。公平地说，在这两种情况下，我们都观察到参与者“使用语言”。然而，还是有区别的。两岁孩子的交流活动的基础是开发高度复杂的声音和结构系统的能力，加上一套计算程序，这将使孩子能够产生包含潜在无限数量的新颖话语的扩展话语。在这个意义上，还没有观察到其他生物“使用语言”。正是在这个更基本或更抽象的意义上，我们说语言是人类独有的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 11. What can we learn from the two attempts in Para. 2?
paragraphs.translationZh: 11. 我们可以从段落中的两次尝试中学到什么？ 2？

paragraphs.translationZh: 12. 以下关于瓦肖和莎拉的陈述哪一项是不正确的？

paragraphs.sourceText: 14.What is the topic of the passage?
paragraphs.translationZh: 14.本文的主题是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) It was well past midnight this past July and the round-the-clock Arctic sun was shining on Mercy Bay. Exhausted Parks Canada archaeologist Ryan Harris was experiencing a rare moment of rest on the rocky beach, looking out over the bay’s dark, ice-studded water. Around him, a dozen red-and-yellow tents lined the shoreline — the only signs of life. Every day for the previous two weeks, work had started by mid-morning and continued nonstop for 16 hours. Night and day had little relevance in the murky, near-freezing waters. Along with Parks Canada’s chief of underwater archaeology, Marc-Andre Bernier, Harris has overseen more than 100 dives at this remote inlet of Banks Island in Aulavik National Park, exploring the wreck of HMS Investigator, a British vessel that has sat on the bottom of the bay for more than 160 years.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 今年七月已经过了午夜，全天候的北极阳光照耀着慈悲湾。疲惫不堪的加拿大公园考古学家瑞安·哈里斯（Ryan Harris）在岩石海滩上享受着难得的休息时刻，眺望着海湾漆黑、布满冰块的海水。在他周围，十几个红黄相间的帐篷排列在海岸线上——这是唯一的生命迹象。前两周，每天中午开始工作，不间断地持续 16 个小时。在浑浊、接近冰冻的水域中，白天和黑夜几乎没有什么关系。哈里斯与加拿大公园管理局水下考古主管马克-安德烈·伯尼尔 (Marc-Andre Bernier) 一起，在奥拉维克国家公园班克斯岛的这个偏远入口处监督了 100 多次潜水，探索英国皇家海军调查号 (HMS Investigator) 的残骸，这艘英国船只已在海湾底部沉睡了 160 多年。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) Harris and a small team of archaeologists had discovered Investigator in 2010 and returned in 2011 with a larger team to dive, study, and document the wreck, which holds a critical place in the history of Arctic exploration. Twenty-five feet below the surface, Investigator sits upright, intact, and remarkably well preserved. Silt covers everything below the main deck, entombing the officers’ cabins, the ship’s galley, and a full library. The archaeologists had intended to leave the wreck and its artifacts where they had lain since the polar ship was abandoned, trapped in ice, on June 3, 1853. Artifact recovery was not part of their original plan, but that plan changed after their first few dives.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 哈里斯和一小队考古学家于 2010 年发现了调查号，并于 2011 年带着更大的团队返回，对这艘沉船进行潜水、研究和记录，该沉船在北极探险史上占有重要地位。调查员在地表以下二十五英尺处直立而立，完好无损，保存得非常完好。淤泥覆盖了主甲板以下的一切，埋葬了军官舱、船上的厨房和一个完整的图书馆。考古学家原本打算将沉船及其文物留在自 1853 年 6 月 3 日这艘极地船被遗弃并困在冰中以来一直存放的地方。文物打捞并不是他们最初计划的一部分，但在他们最初的几次潜水后，这个计划发生了变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) The team was instantly surprised by the number of artifacts they saw — muskets (火枪), shoes, and hunks of copper sheathing rested on Investigator’s upper deck, dangled off the hull, or lay haphazardly on the sediment. Leaving these artifacts behind in Mercy Bay would have made them vulnerable to the icebergs that regularly scour the bay’s floor, including the ones the six-man dive team had been dodging since their arrival.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 团队立即对他们看到的文物数量感到惊讶——火枪、鞋子和大块铜护套放在调查号的上甲板上，悬挂在船体上，或者随意地躺在沉积物上。如果将这些文物留在仁慈湾，它们很容易受到定期冲刷海湾底部的冰山的攻击，其中包括六人潜水队抵达后一直在躲避的冰山。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) Each piece fished from the water was a clue to life at sea aboard a ship during a period of British fervor for Arctic exploration. The captain of Investigator, Robert McClure, was originally sent to find and rescue two ships, HIMS Erebus and HMS Terror, that Sir John Franklin had led into the Arctic in 1845 to discover the long-sought Northwest Passage connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. Investigator’s voyage ended, without sight or word of Franklin’s ships or crew, when it was set upon by ice in Mercy Bay. After 39 months at sea, the listing ship sat, slowly being crushed on all sides, for three frigid years — with no Inuit encounters, no British search parties, and no relief. For much of that time, McClure and his crew of 60 were desperate and under constant threat of starvation, until a surprising rescue in the spring of 1853. Fifty-five men survived the ordeal.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 每一件从水中打捞上来的碎片都是英国热衷北极探险时期船上海上生活的线索。调查者号的船长罗伯特·麦克卢尔最初被派去寻找并营救约翰·富兰克林爵士于 1845 年带领进入北极的两艘船：HIMS Erebus 号和 HMS Terror 号，以发现人们长期以来寻找的连接大西洋和太平洋的西北航道。当调查员号在仁慈湾被冰覆盖时，调查员的航行结束了，没有看到或没有任何关于富兰克林的船只或船员的消息。在海上航行了 39 个月后，这艘倾斜的船静静地坐着，慢慢地从四面八方被压碎，长达三年寒冷的时间——没有遇到因纽特人，没有英国搜索队，也没有救援。在那段时间的大部分时间里，麦克卢尔和他的 60 名船员都处于绝望之中，并持续面临饥饿的威胁，直到 1853 年春天的一次令人惊讶的救援。55 名船员在这场磨难中幸存下来。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) In July 2010, after months of study to pinpoint Investigator’s resting place, the actual discovery of the wreck took just a few minutes. Harris was in the bay in an inflatable boat testing sonar equipment when the wreck came into range. The four hours of video gathered on that trip showed that the ship was, in essence, frozen in time, protected by the cold water and opaque, light-blocking ice cover. It would be a year before they could return with cold-water diving equipment to have a closer, more detailed look. Over that year, the Parks Canada team pored over photographs and examined glowing gold ultrasound images that showed timber from the wreck scattered across the upper deck like matchsticks. They sought and received the blessing for a more intensive exploration of the wreck site from the 136 residents of Sachs Harbour, an Inuvialuit (Inuit from the western Arctic) community on the southwestern tip of Banks Island, the closest permanent community, some 125 miles away. In addition to the underwater work to document the wreck, archaeologist Henry Cary led a land-based survey and excavation team of Inuvialuit archaeologists, conservation officers, and park staff. It fell upon Cary to shuttle the 8,820 pounds of equipment up to the 74th parallel, including tents, a three-week supply of food, two boats, diving gear, compressors, recording equipment, surveying tools, and 20 barrels for collecting fresh drinking water.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 2010年7月，经过数月的研究以确定调查员的安息地点，沉船的实际发现只花了几分钟。当沉船进入范围时，哈里斯正在海湾的一艘充气船上测试声纳设备。那次旅行中收集的四个小时的视频显示，这艘船本质上是被及时冻结的，受到冷水和不透明、遮光的冰盖的保护。他们需要一年的时间才能带着冷水潜水设备回来进行更近距离、更详细的观察。那一年，加拿大公园管理局的团队仔细研究了照片，并检查了发光的金色超声波图像，这些图像显示沉船中的木材像火柴棍一样散落在上层甲板上。他们向萨克斯港 (Sachs Harbour) 的 136 名居民寻求并得到了对沉船地点进行更深入探索的祝福，萨克斯港 (Sachs Harbour) 是一个位于班克斯岛 (Banks Island) 西南端的因纽特人 (来自北极西部的因纽特人) 社区，距离班克斯岛 (Banks Island) 是最近的永久社区，距离约 125 英里。除了记录沉船的水下工作外，考古学家亨利·卡里还领导了一支由因纽特人考古学家、保护官员和公园工作人员组成的陆地调查和挖掘小组。卡里负责将 8,820 磅的设备运送到北纬 74 度线，其中包括帐篷、三周的食物供应、两艘船、潜水装备、压缩机、记录设备、测量工具和 20 个用于收集新鲜饮用水的桶。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) The archaeologists came prepared for delays, nasty weather, and polar bears — but they weren’t prepared for the number of artifacts that needed recovery. Harris, Bernier, Cary, and their crews had packed cameras, lasers, and measuring tapes to document the sites but fewer items to help them retrieve, excavate, or transfer artifacts. Recovering the wreck’s finds quickly used up their small toolkit for stabilizing artifacts: foam padding, tongue depressors, and gauze bandages.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 考古学家们为延误、恶劣天气和北极熊做好了准备，但他们没有为需要打捞的文物数量做好准备。哈里斯、伯尼尔、卡里和他们的工作人员配备了相机、激光和卷尺来记录这些遗址，但帮助他们检索、挖掘或转移文物的物品却很少。打捞沉船残骸很快就用完了他们用来稳定文物的小工具：泡沫垫、压舌板和纱布绷带。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) “We had not really envisioned the number of artifacts that were visible and exposed on the deck. So, basically, we had to improvise,” says Bernier.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) “我们并没有真正预见到甲板上可见和暴露的文物数量。所以，基本上，我们必须即兴创作，”伯尼尔说。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) Someone ripped the lid of a large black storage case off its hinges to use as a cradle to lift a bent and corroded musket from the frigid waters. A large food cooler was loaded with a shredded, twisted, oxidized sample of the copper sheathing used by the British navy to reinforce their Arctic fleet for contact with icebergs. To protect a fragile rectangle of encrusted felt — a novel addition to Investigator that was intended to keep the ship watertight — Harris fashioned a cover out of absorbent chamois (鹿皮), ripped up an old black T-shirt to place underneath it, and sandwiched the artifact between floorboards taken from the boat that had shuttled them between land and the wreck. The artifacts then made a more than 4,000-mile journey, by helicopter and commercial airliner, to the Parks Canada conservation lab in Ottawa, where they are being conserved and studied today.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 有人把一个黑色大储物箱的盖子从铰链上撕下来，用作摇篮，从寒冷的水中抬起弯曲且腐蚀的步枪。一个大型食品冷藏箱中装有英国海军用来加固其北极舰队与冰山接触的破碎、扭曲、氧化的铜护套样品。为了保护易碎的长方形结垢毛毡——这是调查者号的一项新颖补充，旨在保持船的水密性——哈里斯用吸水性的麂皮（鹿皮）制作了一个盖子，撕下一件旧的黑色T恤放在它下面，然后将这件物品夹在从在陆地和沉船之间穿梭的船上取下的地板之间。随后，这些文物搭乘直升机和商用客机，经过 4,000 多英里的旅程，抵达位于渥太华的加拿大公园管理局保护实验室，目前正在那里进行保护和研究。

paragraphs.sourceText: 19. The last paragraph mentions all the following EXCEPT ______
paragraphs.translationZh: 19. 最后一段提到了以下所有内容，除了 ______

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) My father was, I am sure, intended by nature to be a cheerful, kindly man. Until he was thirty-four years old he worked as a farmhand for a man named Thomas Butterworth whose place lay near the town of Bidwell. He had then a horse of his own and on Saturday evenings drove into town to spend a few hours in social intercourse with other farmhands. In town he drank several glasses of beer and stood about in Ben Head’s saloon — crowded on Saturday evenings with visiting farmhands. Songs were sung and glasses thumped on the bar. At ten o’clock father drove home along a lonely country road, made his horse comfortable for the night and himself went to bed, quite happy in his position in life. He had at that time no notion of trying to rise in the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 我确信，我父亲生来就是一个开朗、善良的人。在他三十四岁之前，他一直为一个名叫托马斯·巴特沃斯的人当农场工人，他的住所位于比德韦尔镇附近。当时他有一匹属于自己的马，每周六晚上他都会开车进城，与其他农场工人进行几个小时的社交活动。在城里，他喝了几杯啤酒，然后在本·海德的酒吧里闲逛——每周六晚上，这里都挤满了来访的农场工人。歌声响起，酒杯重重地敲击吧台。十点钟，父亲驱车沿着一条僻静的乡间小路回家，让他的马舒服地过夜，然后他自己就上床睡觉了，对自己在生活中的地位感到非常满意。那时他并没有想要出人头地的念头。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) It was in the spring of his thirty-fifth year that father married my mother, then a country school teacher, and in the following spring I came wriggling and crying into the world. Something happened to the two people. They became ambitious. The passion for getting up in the world took possession of them.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 父亲三十五岁那年春天，与我母亲结婚，当时我母亲是一名乡村学校的老师，第二年春天，我蠕动着、哭着来到了这个世界。两个人发生了一些事情。他们变得雄心勃勃。他们充满了闯荡世界的热情。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) It may have been that mother was responsible. Being a school teacher she had no doubt read books and magazines. She had, I presume, read of how some people rose from poverty to fame and greatness and as I lay beside her — in the days of her lying-in — she may have dreamed that I would someday rule men and cities. At any rate she induced father to give up his place as a farmhand, sell his horse and embark on an independent enterprise of his own. She was a tall silent woman with a long nose and troubled grey eyes. For herself she wanted nothing. For father and myself she was incurably ambitious.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 可能是母亲的责任。作为一名学校老师，她无疑会阅读书籍和杂志。我想，她读过一些人如何从贫穷走向名声和伟大的故事，当我躺在她身边时——在她产假的日子里——她可能梦想着有一天我会统治人类和城市。无论如何，她诱使父亲放弃了农场工人的职位，卖掉了马，开始了自己的独立事业。她是一位身材高大、沉默寡言的女人，长着长鼻子，灰色的眼睛里充满了不安。对于她自己来说，她什么都不想要。对于父亲和我自己来说，她野心勃勃。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) The first venture into which the two people went turned out badly. They rented ten acres of poor stony land on Griggs’s Road, eight miles from Bidwell, and launched into chicken raising. I grew into boyhood on the place and got my first impressions of life there. From the beginning they were impressions of disaster and if, in my turn, I am a gloomy man inclined to see the darker side of life, I attribute it to the fact that what should have been for me the happy joyous days of childhood were spent on a chicken farm.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 两人的第一次创业结果很糟糕。他们在距离比德韦尔八英里的格里格斯路租了十英亩贫瘠的石地，开始养鸡。我在这个地方长大并获得了对那里生活的第一印象。从一开始，它们就给我留下了灾难的印象，如果我是一个阴郁的人，倾向于看到生活的阴暗面，我会将其归因于这样一个事实：对我来说，本应是幸福快乐的童年时光却在养鸡场度过了。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) One unversed in such matters can have no notion of the many and tragic things that can happen to a chicken. It is born out of an egg, lives for a few weeks as a tiny fluffy thing such as you will see pictured on Easter cards, then becomes hideously naked, eats quantities of corn and meal bought by the sweat of your father’s brow, gets diseases called pip, cholera, and other names, stands looking with stupid eyes at the sun, becomes sick and dies. A few hens and now and then a rooster, intended to serve God’s mysterious ends, struggle through to maturity. The hens lay eggs out of which come other chickens and the dreadful cycle is thus made complete. It is all unbelievably complex. Most philosophers must have been raised on chicken farms. One hopes for so much from a chicken and is so dreadfully disillusioned. Small chickens, just setting out on the journey of life, look so bright and alert and they are in fact so dreadfully stupid. They are so much like people they mix one up in one’s judgments of life. If disease does not kill them they wait until your expectations are thoroughly aroused and then walk under the wheels of a wagon — to go squashed and dead back to their maker. Vermin infest their youth, and fortunes must be spent for curative powders.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 不熟悉这些事情的人不可能了解一只鸡可能发生的许多悲惨的事情。它从鸡蛋中诞生，像复活节贺卡上画的那样毛茸茸的小东西能活几个星期，然后变得可怕地赤身裸体，吃掉大量用你父亲汗水买来的玉米和面粉，患上称为皮疹、霍乱和其他名字的疾病，站着用愚蠢的眼睛看着太阳，生病然后死。几只母鸡，偶尔还有一只公鸡，旨在服务于上帝的神秘目的，努力奋斗直至成熟。母鸡产下鸡蛋，鸡蛋又生出其他的鸡，可怕的循环就这样完成了。这一切都复杂得令人难以置信。大多数哲学家一定是在养鸡场长大的。人们对一只鸡抱有如此多的希望，但最后却大失所望。刚刚踏上人生旅程的小鸡，看上去那么聪明机敏，其实却愚蠢得可怕。他们非常像人，以至于在对生活的判断中混为一谈。如果疾病没有杀死它们，它们就会等到你的期望被彻底激发，然后走在马车的轮子下——被压扁，死回到它们的制造者那里。害虫在他们的青春期肆虐，必须花大量的钱来购买治疗粉末。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) For ten years my father and mother struggled to make our chicken farm pay and then they gave up that struggle and began another. They decided to move into the town of Bidwell, and embarked in the restaurant business. 5
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 十年来，我的父亲和母亲一直在努力让我们的养鸡场赚钱，然后他们放弃了这场斗争，开始了另一场斗争。他们决定搬进比德韦尔镇，开始从事餐饮业。 5

paragraphs.sourceText: After ten years of worry with incubators that did not hatch, and with tiny — and in their own way lovely — balls of fluff that passed on into semi-naked pullethood and from that into dead henhood, we threw all aside, packed our belongings on a wagon and drove down Griggs’s Road toward Bidwell, a tiny caravan of hope looking for a new place from which to start on our upward journey through life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经过十年的担心，孵化器没有孵化，微小的——以它们自己的方式可爱——绒毛球会变成半裸的小母鸡，再从那里变成死母鸡。我们把一切都扔到一边，把我们的行李装上马车，沿着格里格斯路开往比德韦尔，这是一支充满希望的小车队，寻找一个新的地方，从那里开始我们人生的向上旅程。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) We must have been a sad looking lot, not, I fancy, unlike refugees fleeing from a battlefield. Mother and I walked in the road. The wagon that contained our goods had been borrowed for the day from Mr. Albert Griggs, a neighbor. Out of its sides stuck the legs of cheap chairs and at the back of the pile of beds, tables, and boxes filled with kitchen utensils was a crate of live chickens, and on top of that the baby carriage in which I had been wheeled about in my infancy. Why we stuck to the baby carriage I don’t know. It was unlikely other children would be born and the wheels were broken. People who have few possessions cling tightly to those they have. That is one of the facts that make life so discouraging.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 我们一定是一群悲伤的人，我想，不像逃离战场的难民。我和妈妈走在路上。装着我们货物的马车是从邻居阿尔伯特·格里格斯先生那里借来的。床、桌子和装满厨房用具的盒子堆在后面，里面放着一箱活鸡，上面放着一辆婴儿车，我小时候就用它来推过。我不知道为什么我们要坚持婴儿车。其他孩子不太可能出生，轮子也坏了。拥有的东西很少的人会紧紧抓住自己拥有的东西。这是让生活如此令人沮丧的事实之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) Father rode on top of the wagon. He was then a bald-headed man of forty-five, a little fat and from long association with mother and the chickens he had become habitually silent and discouraged. All during our ten years on the chicken farm he had worked as a laborer on neighboring farms and most of the money he had earned had been spent for remedies to cure chicken diseases. There were two little patches of hair on father’s head just above his ears. I remember that as a child I used to sit looking at him when he had gone to sleep in a chair before the stove on Sunday afternoons in the winter. I had at that time already begun to read books and have notions of my own and the bald path that led over the top of his head was, I fancied, something like a broad road, such a road as Caesar might have made on which to lead his legions out of Rome and into the wonders of an unknown world.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 父亲骑在马车顶上。那时他是个四十五岁的秃头男人，有点胖，由于长期与母亲和鸡打交道，他习惯性地沉默寡言，灰心丧气。我们在养鸡场的十年里，他一直在邻近的农场当工人，他赚的大部分钱都花在了治疗鸡病的药物上。父亲头上耳朵上方有两小块头发。我记得小时候，冬天的周日下午，当他在炉子前的椅子上睡觉时，我常常坐在那儿看着他。那时我已经开始读书，有了自己的想法，我想，那条通往他头顶的光秃秃的小路就像一条宽阔的道路，凯撒可能会在这条道路上带领他的军团离开罗马，进入一个未知世界的奇迹。

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) One might write a book concerning our flight from the chicken farm into town. Mother and I walked the entire eight miles — she to be sure that nothing fell from the wagon and I to see the wonders of the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 有人可能会写一本关于我们从养鸡场飞往城镇的书。母亲和我走了整整八英里——她是为了确保没有任何东西从马车上掉下来，而我是为了看到世界的奇迹。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Convenience of Online Learning
paragraphs.translationZh: 在线学习的便利性

paragraphs.sourceText: With the widespread use of the computer and the smartphone, an increasing number of people tend to use the Internet to get information and acquire knowledge, which is quite convenient. However, about ten to twenty years ago, when people wanted to learn a language, they had to endure hours of school lessons or evening classes, with their heads buried in textbooks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着电脑和智能手机的广泛使用，越来越多的人倾向于使用互联网获取信息、获取知识，非常方便。然而，大约十到二十年前，当人们想要学习一门语言时，他们必须埋头苦读课本，忍受数小时的学校课程或晚自习。

paragraphs.sourceText: Nowadays, technology appears to be providing a better and more accessible way of learning languages. Having a smartphone means you can have a virtual teacher with you wherever you go. One of the many popular APPs offers 91 courses in 30 languages and has more than 300 million users. Whatever you want to learn, language-learning APPs allow you to go at your own pace and fit learning around other commitments.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如今，技术似乎提供了一种更好、更容易的语言学习方式。拥有智能手机意味着您无论走到哪里都可以有一位虚拟老师陪伴您。其中一款热门APP提供30种语言的91门课程，拥有超过3亿用户。无论您想学什么，语言学习应用程序都可以让您按照自己的节奏进行学习，并围绕其他任务进行学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many schools in China have adopted online platforms to teach classes. In most cases, these platforms employ adaptive learning techniques which customize the learning experience based on each student’s needs, interests, and learning styles. This personalized approach convinces people of the effectiveness of online learning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 中国许多学校都采用网络平台进行教学。在大多数情况下，这些平台采用自适应学习技术，根据每个学生的需求、兴趣和学习风格定制学习体验。这种个性化的方法让人们相信在线学习的有效性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Problems Concerning Online Education
paragraphs.translationZh: 在线教育的问题

paragraphs.sourceText: Technology has accelerated the wide spread of online education, which appears to be more accessible and more convenient compared with traditional education. However, there are also problems concerning online education. Some people may ask, for example, how can one learn subjects such as chemistry without being able to use the laboratory equipment, how can one learn a language without face-to-face interaction involving gestures, facial expressions, body postures, and how can one meet extra-curricular requirements, such as forming good habits, holding up social norms and keeping high standards of discipline if they are stuck behind a computer monitor? There are many issues that need to be addressed if online education is to thrive.
paragraphs.translationZh: 技术加速了在线教育的广泛普及，与传统教育相比，在线教育显得更加便捷。但在线教育也存在一些问题。例如，有人会问，如果没有实验室设备，如何学习化学等科目；如果没有手势、面部表情、身体姿势等面对面的互动，如何学习一门语言；如果被困在电脑显示器后面，如何满足课外要求，例如养成良好的习惯、遵守社会规范、保持高标准的纪律？在线教育要蓬勃发展，有许多问题需要解决。

paragraphs.sourceText: Professor Smith, department head of modern languages at River University, argues that technology never spells the end of traditional classrooms and teachers. She says that teaching APPs should be used alongside conventional classroom methods, not to the exclusion of traditional teaching. And she adds, “The APPs are not designed for degrees, but they could be additional resources.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 河大学现代语言系主任史密斯教授认为，技术永远不会意味着传统教室和教师的终结。她表示，教学APP应该与传统课堂教学方式结合起来，而不是排斥传统教学。她补充道，“这些应用程序不是为学位而设计的，但它们可以成为额外的资源。”

A database-management system is a collection of interrelated data and a set of programs to access those data. The collection of data, usually referred to as the database, contain information relevant to an enterprise. Its primary goal is to provide a (1) _______ way to store and retrieve database information.
paragraphs.translationZh: 数据库管理系统是相互关联的数据和一组访问这些数据的程序的集合。数据的集合通常称为数据库，包含与企业相关的信息。它的主要目标是提供一种(1) _______方法来存储和检索数据库信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: Database systems are designing to manage large bodies of information. (2) _______ Management of data involves both defining structures for storage of information and provide mechanisms for its manipulation. In addition, the database system must (3) _______ ensure information safety, despite system crashes or attempts at unauthorized access. If data are to be shared between several users, the system must avoid possible (4) _______ anomalous results. Computer scientists have developed various concepts and techniques for managing data, so information is very important in most organizations. (5) _______
paragraphs.translationZh: 数据库系统旨在管理大量信息。 (2) _______ 数据管理涉及定义信息存储结构并提供信息操作机制。此外，数据库系统必须(3) _______确保信息安全，尽管系统崩溃或尝试未经授权的访问。如果要在多个用户之间共享数据，系统必须避免可能出现的(4) _______异常结果。计算机科学家已经开发了各种管理数据的概念和技术，因此信息在大多数组织中都非常重要。 (5) _______

paragraphs.sourceText: The earliest database systems arose in the 1960s in response to the computerized management of commercial data. Those earlier applications were relatively simple compared with modern database applications, that include highly sophisticated, (6) _______ worldwide enterprises.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最早的数据库系统出现于 20 世纪 60 年代，以应对商业数据的计算机化管理。与现代数据库应用程序相比，那些早期的应用程序相对简单，现代数据库应用程序包括高度复杂的(6) _______全球企业。

paragraphs.sourceText: All database applications share important common elements. The central aspect (7) _______ of the application is the data themselves. Today, some of the most valuable corporations are valuable because of their physical assets, but because of the (8) _______ information they own. Imagine of a bank without its data on accounts and customers (9) _______ or a social-network site that loses connections with their users. Such companies’ value (10)_______ would be almost totally lost under such circumstances.
paragraphs.translationZh: 所有数据库应用程序都共享重要的共同元素。应用程序的核心部分(7) _______是数据本身。如今，一些最有价值的公司之所以有价值，不仅是因为它们的有形资产，还因为它们拥有的 (8) _______ 信息。想象一下，一家银行没有账户和客户数据(9) _______，或者一个社交网站失去了与用户的联系。在这种情况下，这些公司的价值(10)_______几乎会完全消失。
